     - Decisions start with "Decision needed", give the options with their costs and my pick, and end with "?".
     - Mark proposals as proposals.
     - Stay under about 500 words.
     - Test end to end.

# header, uses the clang-tidy on your system or installs the pinned one into a
# virtual environment inside it, and runs scripts/clang_tidy_diff.py the way CI
# does. Uncommitted changes are checked too.

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh [options]

  -b, --base REV       revision to compare against (default: main of the remote that
                       points at OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer, else origin/main)
      --no-fetch       do not fetch that remote's main first
  -B, --build-dir DIR  build directory for the compile database (default: build-tidy)
  -d, --deps-dir DIR   dependency build directory (default: deps/build on Linux,
                       deps/build/<arch> on macOS)
  -j, --jobs N         parallel clang-tidy runs (default: all cores)
      --fix            apply clang-tidy's fixes (adds the missing includes)
  -y, --yes            install missing tools without asking; another clang-tidy
                       version found on the system is then not offered
  -h, --help           show this help
EOF
}

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
cd "$ROOT"

BASE=""
FETCH=1
BUILD_DIR=build-tidy
DEPS_DIR=""
JOBS=""
FIX=0
YES=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        -b|--base) BASE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --no-fetch) FETCH=0; shift ;;
        -B|--build-dir) BUILD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        -d|--deps-dir) DEPS_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        -j|--jobs) JOBS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --fix) FIX=1; shift ;;
        -y|--yes) YES=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
done

case "$BUILD_DIR" in
    /*) ;;
    *) BUILD_DIR="$ROOT/$BUILD_DIR" ;;
esac

content.text:
You're right. Before your message, I had tested crash reports but hadn't signed in or out by hand, sent an ordinary error report, or run the lint. I've done all three now, and they turned up two real problems. Neither JusPrin change is landed yet because of the second one.

**What the tests showed.** I used the test build against the local server, with reports going to a stand-in Sentry on this Mac.

- **Signing in by hand** with the emailed code saved account number 77. An ordinary error report sent while signed in named the person `77` and carried the install id tag.
- **Signing out by hand** in Preferences erased the saved number. The next ordinary report named the install id, and so did a crash right after.
- **The lint check** failed. `AgentConfiguration.cpp` called `account_provider()` without directly including the header that declares it. I added the include, the lint now passes, and all 627 agent test cases pass. That fix is a second commit on the branch `claude/sentry-user-id`.
- **The real problem:** the error-report dialog tells people "The report is anonymous: it has no chat messages, no files and nothing that says who you are." Preferences › Updates says the same. With this change, every report now carries the account number or the install id, so that promise is false.

**Committed:** the Sentry triage notes, in the devops repo on main (a365dbd).

**The stuck chat (OBICO-SERVER-B2N) is reproduced.** I added a test that feeds the app's real code the two server replies from the captured chat, then stops the turn while the app is answering the second reply's tool calls. The next message's request carries the web search with no result. That's the same history Anthropic refused in the Sentry issue. The test fails today, which is the bug, and I saved it at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-claude-cowork-wd/acec8758-e267-4d72-9bfa-8a20ffd3d65e/scratchpad/b2n-repro-test.patch`. The cause is that the app saves a reply only after it has sent that reply's tool results back. A stopped or failed turn never sends them, so the whole second reply is lost, search result included.

**Decision needed: should I change the anonymous-report wording before landing?** It's your call because it's what JusPrin promises people about their privacy. There are three options:

- **Reword before landing (my pick).** Change the dialog and the Preferences text to say a report carries your account number, or this install's id if you're not signed in, but no name or email. Also add that id as a line under "See what the report contains". This adds one more change and the translation update. I'd do the cold-reader check from the JusPrin design guidelines first.
- **Land as is and reword later.** The text stays false until the rewording ships.
- **Send only the install id.** This undoes your choice of the account number, and I'd argue the install id still identifies an install.

**Decision needed: should I fix the stuck chat this way?** When a turn ends before the app has answered every tool call in a reply, the app would still save that reply. It would answer each unanswered call as "not run: the turn was stopped", using the same "not run" answer it already gives in other cases. The search result is then kept, and every call has a result. The other option is to strip the unanswered search from the history before sending, which is simpler but loses what the search found. My pick is the first. Should I go ahead with it?

The change is landed on jusprin-dev in the main JusPrin checkout, `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`, as one commit, bc68055371. It contains the change and the include fix that made the lint pass. I wrote it as a single commit for two reasons. The first commit's message ran its whole first paragraph into the subject line. And its "Not tested" list was out of date, because the commit message now lists everything tested today. It isn't pushed. I removed the worktree and its branch after confirming the landed commit has exactly the same code as the branch.

**Decision needed: should I fix the stuck chat (OBICO-SERVER-B2N) this way?** The test that reproduces it is saved at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-claude-cowork-wd/acec8758-e267-4d72-9bfa-8a20ffd3d65e/scratchpad/b2n-repro-test.patch`. Today, when a turn is stopped or fails while the app is still answering an AI reply's tool calls, that reply is never saved. If the reply carried a web search's result, the next message sends the search with no result, and Anthropic refuses the request.

- **Answer the unanswered calls as "not run" (my pick).** The app saves the reply anyway and answers each unanswered call as "not run: the turn was stopped". That's the same kind of "not run" answer it already gives in other cases. The search result is kept, and every call has a result.
- **Strip the unanswered search.** Remove the search that has no result from the history before sending. That's simpler, but the model loses what the search found.

Should I go ahead with answering the calls as "not run"?

Another Claude session sent a message:
<cross-session-message from="local_9480cf71-704b-42b9-a20d-b65dec5c087f" from-name="btw: What's the nature of this bug in plain English?">
Kenneth approved the full fix for the stuck chat (OBICO-SERVER-B2N) in the JusPrin app; please implement it on a new branch from jusprin-dev.

Kenneth's words, in reply to "should I go ahead with the full fix?": "yes. but tell the main sessino to do it."

What a forked session found since your last turn:

1. Root cause, confirmed by Anthropic's docs (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools, section "Mixing server tools and client tools in one turn") and by a live test. When one AI reply asks for both a web search and an app tool, Anthropic stops with stop_reason "tool_use" and does not run the search yet. The reply holds a server_tool_use with no result. Once the app sends back a message holding ONLY tool_result blocks, Anthropic runs the search, and the next reply starts with the web_search_tool_result. ProviderAgent saves a reply only after its tool results are sent (m_settled). So a turn stopped while the app is answering the second reply's calls loses that reply, search result included. The next message then carries a search with no result, and Anthropic refuses it with 400.

2. Live test against the real Anthropic API: claude-sonnet-5-5 and web_search_20250305, the same model and tool version the app uses, called with the local server's JUSPRIN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The script is at /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-claude-cowork-wd/1cc36343-d411-49df-8068-d161345f2791/scratchpad/b2n_live.py, run inside the web container. Results:
   - Second reply lost, then tool results plus the person's new text: 400 "`web_search` tool use with id … was found without a corresponding `web_search_tool_result` block". This is the B2N error, reproduced.
   - Second reply kept, then the new message: 200.
   - Turn stopped after the FIRST reply, search block kept, "not run" stand-in tool_results plus new text: 400, same error. The search never ran, so no result exists anywhere. Stand-ins alone are not enough.
   - Turn stopped after the first reply, server_tool_use with no result DROPPED, stand-in tool_result plus new text: 200.
   - Not covered: in this run the second reply had no further tool_use, so stand-ins after a kept second reply were not exercised directly. Stand-in tool_results are accepted in the case above.

3. The approved fix ("full fix"):
   - Save every reply as it arrives, instead of only after its tool results are sent.
   - When building the next request, answer every unanswered app tool_use with a stand-in result: failed, "Not run: the turn was stopped". This follows the existing "not_run" answer style in ProviderAgent::next_call.
   - Drop any server_tool_use, such as web_search, that has no matching result block, because it never ran.
   - Research showed this matches common practice: Claude Code, OpenClaw and agent-sdk use synthetic "cancelled" results; Vercel AI SDK treats a call as resolved once a result is in the history. No project found waits to save until a reply is fully answered.
   - Check whether the current rule "nothing is saved from a request the provider refused" (record() runs on the first stream event) still needs keeping.

4. Reproduction test, which fails today: /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-claude-cowork-wd/acec8758-e267-4d72-9bfa-8a20ffd3d65e/scratchpad/b2n-repro-test.patch. Its sequence is: reply 1 has a search plus a call; reply 2 has the search result plus two calls; then cancel(); then a new message. It checks that the next request carries the search result. Make it pass, and add a case where the turn stops right after reply 1 and the unrun search is dropped.

The stuck-chat fix is written and passes all the offline tests, but I haven't committed it. I'm holding it until the live Anthropic tests have run, and those need your OK. It's in the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/b2n-stuck-chat`, on the branch `claude/b2n-stuck-chat`, made from jusprin-dev.

**What changed:**
- **Each AI reply is saved the moment it arrives**, instead of only after the app has sent back the results of its tool calls. A turn that stops in the middle still keeps the reply, including a web search result it carried.
- **When the next message is built, every tool call left without a result gets a stand-in result.** It's marked failed with the code `turn_ended`.
- **A web search that never got a result anywhere in the chat is left out**, because it never ran. Inside a turn that's still going, the search is kept, because Anthropic only runs it once the app's results come back.

One difference from the plan the side session described: the stand-in says "the turn ended before this call's result was sent back. It may or may not have run", not "Not run". The app may already have carried out a call, such as applying a settings change, before the person pressed stop. Saying it didn't run could lead the AI to apply the change a second time.

**Tested so far:**
- I added two tests that run the app's real Anthropic code on the server replies from the captured chat. In the first, the turn stops after the reply carrying the search result. In the second, it stops before the search ran, and the app starts the next turn on its own note with no text from the person. Both failed before the fix and pass now.
- All 629 agent test cases pass. Two existing record tests and one bridge test now expect the reply to be saved and a stand-in result in the next message. I changed those expectations on purpose, because they described the old behaviour.
- Lint passes against jusprin-dev.

**Decision needed: should I run the two new live tests against the real Anthropic API?** They go through the app's real code. Each one asks Claude for a web search and an app tool call at once, stops the turn at one of the two points, then checks that Anthropic accepts the next message. They also turn on Anthropic's strictest check that past AI reasoning is replayed unchanged. That matters because leaving out a search that never ran edits a saved reply. The offline tests can't answer that; only Anthropic can. The project's live-test rules say a run needs your approval first. Each test stops itself before spending more than $0.50, and I expect about $0.10 to $0.30 each on Opus 5.5. They'd use the Anthropic key from the local server, as the side session did. The program that runs them is still building.

person's reports from before and after signing in can be matched.

without it is unexpected and stores nothing. Signing out erases it and the
